source.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States

accepted.question_text: For a translationally invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on an L by L torus defined by a local tensor A, let R be a square region and let H be the parent Hamiltonian obtained by translating the local projector associated to R. What are the weakest conditions on the tensor A, and how small can the region R be chosen, that guarantee the resulting PEPS is the unique ground state of H and that H has a nonzero spectral gap?

Let T be a primitive quantum channel acting on D by D matrices, where the primitivity index p(T) is the smallest positive integer n such that T raised to the n-th power sends every positive semidefinite input to a full-rank matrix. What is the exact best possible upper bound on p(T) as a function of D?

For a normal translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index, meaning the smallest scale at which the associated tensor becomes injective?
For a normal projected entangled pair state (PEPS) with bond dimension D, what is the exact best possible upper bound, in terms of D alone, for its injectivity index?

Find an explicit computable function f(D), preferably polynomial in the PEPS bond dimension D, that upper-bounds the injectivity index of every normal projected entangled pair state with bond dimension D.

Is the following bulk-boundary correspondence for PEPS exactly true: the parent Hamiltonian of a projected entangled pair state is gapped if and only if the corresponding boundary states can be written as Gibbs states of one-dimensional short-range Hamiltonians whose interaction terms decay exponentially with distance?

In two dimensions, does every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian admit a global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption alone, without any additional assumption controlling the concentration of low-energy eigenvalues near the ground-state energy?
For the two-dimensional global PEPS approximation problem, can the bond-dimension bound f(L) required to approximate an L by L system be chosen to grow polynomially in the linear system size L?

In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(epsilon) be chosen polynomial in 1/epsilon?

Suppose two local tensors A and B define exactly the same projected entangled pair state on every L by L torus, meaning the PEPS generated by A equals the PEPS generated by B for all system sizes L. What local relation between A and B characterizes this equality of PEPS?

Develop a Fundamental Theorem for PEPS in two and higher dimensions that applies to the largest possible class of projected entangled pair states, bridging the currently understood normal case and the fully general case where equality of generated states is undecidable.

Let A and B be PEPS tensors such that there exist epsilon greater than zero and a size L0 with the property that, for every L at least L0, the states they define on the L by L torus are within squared Hilbert-norm distance epsilon. Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply any local relation between A and B?

For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?
What is the exact computational complexity class of the two-dimensional PEPS zero-testing problem?
Given a finite group G and a normal subgroup H, does there exist a low-depth noisy quantum circuit that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H?
What is the exact relationship between projected entangled pair states and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions?
